FALCON-S

Fixed-wing ground-effect Aerodynamics Simulator and Flight Control Learning Suite

X-Plane render
Airship V7 in ground effect

FALCON-S is a GPU-parallel, six-degree-of-freedom simulator and controller benchmark for fixed-wing aircraft flying close to the ground. It models ground effect, actuator and sensor dynamics and Dryden turbulence across four airframes, and drives reinforcement learning (PPO, SAC, TD3) and classical control (LQR, MPPI) through one command interface and one plant, so a comparison measures the controller and not the task encoding.

Anonymous authors Paper under double-blind review. Code, checkpoints and results are in the anonymized repository.

OverviewAgent module · environment module

One plant, one command interface, five controllers

Simulators built for pilots are hard to run at scale, and simulators built for learning tend to drop the physics that matter near the ground. FALCON-S keeps ground effect, actuator lag, sensor imperfection and turbulence in the loop and still steps tens of millions of environments per second.

Recorded flights2 airframes × 4 maneuvers × 5 controllers

Five controllers fly the same command stream

A maneuver here is a stream of bank, climb-rate and airspeed commands, not a path to follow. All five executors receive the identical stream and drive the same plant. These are recorded simulator tracks. The ribbon spans the wingtips, so it twists as the aircraft banks.

BenchmarkAltitude · attitude · ground effect · robustness

What the benchmark measures

Every cell flies the same airframe, actuator and sensor models and the same reference. Learned methods pool five training seeds, MPPI repeated sampling draws. Errors are the interquartile mean over surviving episodes with a 95 % bootstrap interval, and survival is reported with its own interval, so no cell hides the runs it lost.

Task 1Altitude acquisition and hold

Reach a commanded altitude, then stay there

Each episode starts 12 to 18 m above or below a target between 20 and 100 m, and every controller follows the same rate-limited reference. Survival: no crash or stall. Acquisition: the target is reached and held within 1 m.

One episode per controller, target 60 m

Single illustrative episodes flown with the shipped checkpoints (first seed; MPPI sampler seed 0). Dashed: the reference, ramping at 2 m/s. Shaded: the ±1 m capture band.

Learned cells pool five seeds × 200 episodes and MPPI three sampling sweeps; the LQR is deterministic and swept once. Learned policies and MPPI fly the GPU plant, the LQR the CPU reference plant, held to single-step parity.

Task 2Attitude-command tracking

Four maneuvers, bank error in degrees

Each command stream comes from its own airframe's envelope, so a maneuver name means a comparable difficulty, not a comparable geometry. A cell gives the bank RMSE over surviving runs, the time inside the ±8.6° band and the runs that departed. Select a cell to fly it above.

lower errorhigher error (log scale)best in column

How far the LQR can bank · one constant-bank turn per angle

Bank RMSE of a constant-bank turn at each commanded angle, held for 1.3 turn periods (at most 120 s). A cell is inside the envelope when the run survives and holds the ±8.6° band 90 % of the time.

Ground effectThrust required against height over span

Near the surface, the same flight costs less thrust

Under a stabilising controller, ground effect changes the thrust needed to fly a trajectory rather than the trajectory itself. Bring the aircraft down toward the water and read the saving at each height-over-span ratio h/b.

Does training in ground effect matter? · 2 × 2 of train GE × evaluation GE

Each PPO altitude policy is fine-tuned twice on a near-ground band, h/b 0.20 to 0.46: once with the correction on, once with it off. Each child is flown with the correction on and off, 200 episodes per cell and seed, and again in a 30 m band to check forgetting.

RobustnessPPO attitude executor · four disturbance families

What breaks the attitude executor

The PPO executor flies the four maneuvers under one disturbance family at a time, at three severities in physical units, 100 realisations per seed, maneuver and severity. Disturbances corrupt what the policy sees or commands; every metric comes from the true state. A second executor, trained with a random action and observation delay of up to 100 ms per episode, flies the same grid.

SimulatorEnvironment module

Inside the plant

Full 6-DoF rigid-body dynamics in a north-east-down frame, with OpenVSP derivative aerodynamics and ground effect, actuator dynamics, configurable sensors and Dryden turbulence. The CPU reference, PyTorch and Warp backends implement the same equations, validated to single-step parity.

Rigid body

mv˙=Fg+Fa+Ft−ω×mv Jω˙=τa+τt−ω×Jω

Newton–Euler equations in the body frame, attitude as a unit quaternion, integrated at Δt = 10 ms with Euler or RK4.

Aerodynamics

Faero=q¯S[−CD,CY,−CL]⊤,q¯=12ρVa2

27 stability and control derivatives from a VSPAERO analysis of each airframe's OpenVSP model, linear about its run point, with a quadratic induced-drag term. Episodes end past the linear range of α; there is no stall model.

Ground effect

c=c∞+Δc(h/c¯) CL(h)=CL(hf)μL(h)μL(hf),h<hf

VSPAERO repeats the analysis with a ground plane at eleven heights, h/b 0.2 to 2, so every derivative moves with height, pitching moment included. Below the lowest height hf the Phillips–Hunsaker lifting-line correlation continues lift and drag. Where both apply they agree within 3 % on lift and drag; either can be selected alone.

Actuators

H(s)=ωn2s2+2ζωns+ωn2,1τs+1

Servos second order at ωn = 10 rad/s, ζ = 1/√2; motors first order with τ = 0.2 s electric and 3 s piston. Saturation at ±20° elevator, ±15° aileron and rudder.

Propulsion

T=12ρSpCpVd(Vd−Va),Vd=Va+δt(km−Va)

Propeller momentum theory with per-airframe constants. Per-motor throttle, mounting and spin direction give differential thrust and torque reaction.

Atmosphere and wind

Lu=Lv=h(0.177+0.000823h)1.2,σw=0.1W20

Dryden turbulence per MIL-F-8785C, scale lengths re-evaluated every step at the current altitude. Constant wind and ISA density. Off during training unless randomisation is requested.

GPU backend performanceRTX 4090 · Ryzen 9 7950X · 10 CUDA-fenced trials

Simulation stops being the bottleneck

The Warp backend scales near-linearly across the widths RL training uses and peaks near 2 × 10⁵ environments before it becomes bandwidth-bound. Simulation then accounts for under 10 % of training wall clock; gradient updates set the rest.

Warp, fused kernels PyTorch, same physics NumPy CPU, one process per env ★ NeuralPlane, published at 10⁶ envs

Cross-simulator validationJSBSim · X-Plane

Checked against two independent simulators

With ground effect off, free-flight trajectories match JSBSim almost exactly. With it on at 1 m, they diverge in the way the physics predicts, because JSBSim does not model ground effect.

JSBSim. Pearson correlation between the two simulators under identical zero-input conditions. The lower airspeed correlation with ground effect on is the altered drag that JSBSim does not reproduce, which isolates the correction as an aerodynamic effect rather than a numerical artefact.

X-Plane. Its flight model is closed, so the test is controller transfer: a controller tuned in FALCON-S is closed around the X-Plane aircraft through XPlaneConnect, from the same configuration and initial conditions. The same interface renders the footage at the top of this page.

Both harnesses are in the repository: tools/jsbsim_validate and tools/xplane.

AirframesJSON configuration · OpenVSP geometry

Four airframes, from a 1.6 m RC plane to a light aircraft

Each airframe is a JSON file: geometry, mass and inertia, control-surface layout, propulsion and sensors. The benchmark tables use the Airship V7, the ground-effect prototype the framework was built around, and the Volantex Ranger, a widely flown electric RC airframe. Wingspans below are drawn to one scale.

Get startedPython 3.10 · CUDA 12.6 · MIT licence

Train, evaluate, reproduce

The Warp plant needs an NVIDIA GPU; falcons check and the NumPy reference plant run without one. Runtimes below are those of the shipped run on an RTX 4090 shared with another job; an idle GPU is faster.

Install
# anonymized repository, as a ZIP
$ curl -L -o falcon-s.zip \
    https://anonymous.4open.science/api/repo/rl-control-wig-aircrafts-1D52/zip
$ unzip falcon-s.zip -d falcon-s && cd falcon-s
$ bash scripts/setup_venv.sh
# venv, lockfile, editable install, falcons check

# or in Docker
$ docker build -t falcons .
$ docker run --rm --gpus all falcons
Train and evaluate
# 3 algorithms × 2 tasks × 4 airframes × any seed
$ scripts/train_seeds.sh          # the 62 shipped runs
$ falcons train --algo ppo --task altitude \
    --plane Airship_V7 --seed 0

# learned or classical, same interface
$ falcons eval --algo ppo --task altitude \
    --plane Airship_V7 --plot
$ falcons eval --algo mppi --task attitude \
    --plane Volantex_Ranger --maneuver circle
Benchmark and reproduce
$ falcons benchmark altitude       # 3 h 35
$ falcons benchmark maneuvers --refresh # 25 min
$ falcons benchmark ground-effect  # 3 min
$ falcons benchmark robustness     # 44 min
$ falcons benchmark ge-training    # 17 min
$ falcons benchmark throughput     # 7 min, idle GPU
$ falcons tables
$ falcons reproduce --out DIR
# re-fly everything, diff against results/
Deterministic rows return bit-identical.Every learned-policy row and every LQR row of the shipped tables re-flies to the same bits from the shipped checkpoints.
Sampling planners are gated by their spread.An MPPI cell is a draw, so each metric carries its own standard deviation and a re-run must land within 3σ of the shipped value.
One inner loop.eval is the loop benchmark composes, so a cell printed by eval is the cell that lands in the table.
